summary: Describes cases where bridging multiple links into a single subnet requires network-layer support, and specifies the IP-layer support that enables bridging in those cases using Neighbor Discovery proxies. It is an experimental protocol.

eli5.summary: Like a go-between passing messages between two rooms so they act like one big room with a single address range.

subtitle: How a device can join two IPv6 links into one subnet at the network layer when ordinary bridging is not possible.

tldr.problem: Classic link-layer bridging needs promiscuous mode and the same kind of link-layer addressing on every port. Wireless client links and PPP links cannot meet that, so people turn to NAT to attach a leaf network.
tldr.mechanism: A proxy forwards packets between its interfaces and rewrites the link-layer addresses inside Neighbor Solicitations, Neighbor Advertisements, Router Advertisements and Redirects to its own address on the outgoing interface. A Proxy bit in Router Advertisements prevents loops.
tldr.outcome: Several segments can share one IPv6 subnet prefix with no change to existing routers. The RFC is Experimental, and it adds no security mechanism of its own for proxied Neighbor Discovery.

facts.label: New flag
facts.value: Proxy (P) bit in the Router Advertisement flags

facts.label: RAs before forwarding
facts.value: 2 P-bit RAs on a downstream interface

today: RFC 4389 is an Experimental RFC. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it, and the text itself leaves secure proxying to future work.

sections.title: Why Bridge at the IP Layer
sections.content:
Bridging several links into one subnet needs only a single subnet prefix and no extra subnet numbers to manage. In IPv4, NATs are often used to attach a leaf link without help from the network provider, but they modify addresses and are problematic for many applications. The goal here is to avoid NAT for IPv6 while still needing no cooperation from the router.

Classic IEEE 802 bridging is preferred whenever it works. It does not work when a port cannot use promiscuous mode, or when ports do not all use IEEE 802 addressing. The RFC targets two such cases. In the first, the upstream link is wireless, where one wireless node cannot see traffic to or from other wireless nodes. In the second, the upstream link is PPP, which is not an 802 medium.

The RFC says it does not apply to topologies with loops or with routers on multiple segments. Those cases are detected and proxying is turned off.
sections.eli5: Normally a go-between just listens to everything and passes it on. In some rooms the go-between cannot hear everything, so it has to learn who is who and speak up for them.

sections.title: What the Proxy Must Achieve
sections.content:
The design goals are to connect multiple segments with one subnet prefix, support media that cannot be bridged at the link layer, and need no changes to existing routers. The proxy must give full connectivity between all nodes in the subnet, prevent loops, work with no routers present, support nodes moving between segments, allow a proxy to be added dynamically, and not break classic bridges already in use.

Some things are explicitly not required, because classic bridges do not provide them either. A proxy need not show up as a hop in a traceroute, use the shortest path, or use all interfaces at once. It also cannot support media where Neighbor Discovery is impossible, such as 6to4, which maps IPv6 addresses to IPv4 addresses algorithmically. Redirects that point to a router on a different segment from the redirected host are out of scope.
sections.eli5: The helper must let everyone talk to everyone, must not make loops of messages, and must not force the grown-ups running the network to change anything.

sections.title: Forwarding Packets
sections.content:
Network-layer proxying SHOULD be used only when classic bridging is not possible. When a proxy interface comes up, the node puts it in all-multicast mode, since many interfaces cannot do full promiscuous mode. Each proxy interface keeps a neighbor cache. For each packet received from a source other than the unspecified address, the proxy looks up the source in that cache and creates a STALE entry if none exists.

Multicast packets of other types are delivered locally as usual and forwarded unchanged, apart from a new link-layer header, out all other proxy interfaces. The Hop Limit is not updated. Unicast packets that are not for the proxy go to the interface whose neighbor entry is in the best state, where the order from least to most preferred is INCOMPLETE, STALE, DELAY, PROBE, REACHABLE. A packet is never sent back out the interface it arrived on. If no cache entry exists, the proxy SHOULD queue the packet and start Neighbor Discovery, or MAY silently drop it.

On each forwarded packet the source link-layer address becomes that of the outgoing interface, the destination becomes the address in the neighbor entry, and any link-layer address inside the payload is replaced with the outgoing interface address. If the outgoing MTU is smaller than the packet, the proxy drops it and sends a Packet Too Big message.
sections.eli5: The helper passes notes from room to room. Each time, it puts its own return address on the envelope, so replies come back to the helper.

sections.title: Proxying Neighbor Discovery and Loop Prevention
sections.content:
Four message types carry link-layer addresses and get special treatment. A Neighbor Solicitation is processed locally but not answered from the proxy's cache; it is proxied onward and the matching advertisement is proxied when it arrives. This keeps hosts that move between segments from being misled. A Neighbor Advertisement first updates the receiving interface's neighbor cache, then is proxied.

For Router Advertisements, the RFC defines a new Proxy bit, P, in the RA flags field. The proxy picks an upstream interface, either by the physical setup or by manual configuration. An RA with P clear arriving upstream is proxied downstream with P set. An interface where an RA with P set arrived within the last 60 minutes MUST NOT be used as a proxy interface. A downstream interface that received any RA in the last 60 minutes MUST NOT be used either. A proxy MUST also wait until it has sent two P-bit RAs on a downstream interface before enabling forwarding there.

For Redirects, the target link-layer address option depends on what the proxy knows. If the target is reachable on the same interface as the redirected host, it carries the target's address. If the target is on another interface, it carries the proxy's own address. If the proxy has no valid entry, the option is left out so the host does its own Neighbor Discovery.

Guidance for future protocols is simple. If a link-layer address in a payload can later appear in a link-layer header, the proxy should substitute its own. If it never will, as with DHCPv6, it should not.
sections.eli5: The helper does not guess answers. It asks the other room and passes the answer back. A special flag on the signs tells other helpers not to join in, so no one ends up passing notes in circles.

sections.title: A Worked Example
sections.content:
Take nodes A and B on separate segments joined by proxy P. A has link-layer address a, B has b, and P has p1 on A's segment and p2 on B's segment.

A sends a Neighbor Solicitation for B, with a in the source link-layer address option. P receives it, records A and an INCOMPLETE entry for B, and proxies it out the other interface with p2 in that option. B replies with an advertisement to p2 carrying b. P marks B as REACHABLE, swaps in p1, and sends it to A. A now believes B is at p1.
sections.eli5: A asks for B. The helper asks B on A's behalf. B answers the helper, and the helper tells A. After that, A sends everything for B to the helper.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Proxies have the same weaknesses as hosts using unsecured Neighbor Discovery, including traffic hijacking and denial of service within the subnet. A proxy is also a legitimate man-in-the-middle, so there is a need to tell proxies apart from attackers.

This RFC adds no new protection. It gives no way to authorize devices as proxies and no extension to SEND to let SEND and proxies work together. Because the proxy's changes invalidate the RSA Signature Option in a secured message, SEND nodes either discard such messages or treat them as unsecured, and the latter is the intended behavior. A rogue Router Advertisement can also make a proxy turn itself off, which is a denial-of-service threat.
sections.eli5: The helper is allowed to pretend to be the sender, but a bad person could pretend to be a helper too, and this document does not give a way to tell them apart.

viz.caption: A RESOLVES B THROUGH PROXY P (RFC 4389, SECTION 5)

messages.label: NS for B (SLLA a)
messages.note: Sent to the solicited-node multicast address for B.

messages.label: NS proxied (SLLA p2)
messages.note: P swaps in its own address on the other segment.

messages.label: NA (TLLA b)
messages.note: Sent to p2, the address B learned for A.

messages.label: NA proxied (TLLA p1)
messages.note: A now records B as reachable at p1.
